findings.title: Every new denied resource now bypasses the permission cache and queries the DB
findings.body:
When cached permissions exist but do not grant access, `Check` falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`. That function no longer consults `permCache`, so it always runs the basic-role, team and permission queries against the DB.

The denial cache only short-circuits repeats of the exact (user, action, name, folder) tuple. A user checked against many distinct resources they cannot access triggers a full permission query per resource, for example when filtering a search result set dashboard by dashboard. Singleflight only dedups concurrent identical calls.

Before this change those checks were served from `permCache`. This can multiply DB load substantially for users with restricted access.

findings.title: Requery does not refresh the stale folder tree, so newly created folders still deny and the denial gets cached
findings.body:
The DB fallback only refreshes the permission scope map. `checkInheritedPermissions` still uses `buildFolderTree`, which is served from `folderCache` (30s TTL).

Scenario: a dashboard sits in a newly created folder whose ancestor grants access. The new folder is missing from the cached tree, so `Ancestors(req.ParentFolder)` yields nothing and the check is denied. That denial is then written to `permDenialCache`, extending the wrong answer.

This is part of the scenario the PR claims to fix (newly created folders) and it remains broken. On a miss, the folder tree should also be refreshed, or the denial should not be cached when the parent folder is absent from the tree.

findings.title: Denial cache pins stale denials for 30s, undermining the 'requery on miss' fix
findings.body:
Any denial is cached for `shortCacheTTL` (30s), and the denial cache is checked before anything else.

If a check for a resource happens before its permissions are written, the denial sticks. This can occur during a create flow or right before a share or grant. Every subsequent check for that resource then returns denied for 30s without consulting the DB, even after the permission exists.

This reintroduces the delay the PR is trying to eliminate for newly created dashboards and folders. Nothing invalidates the entry when permissions are granted.

findings.title: Ambiguous denial cache key can deny unrelated resources
findings.body:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` joins name and parent with `_` and no escaping. Resource names and folder UIDs may legitimately contain underscores.

For example, (name="a_b", parent="") and (name="a", parent="b") produce the same key. A cached denial for one resource then wrongly denies access to the other.

The key also shares the `.perm_` prefix with `userPermCacheKey` in the same cache backend, which increases collision risk with differently typed entries. Use a distinct prefix and an unambiguous separator or encoding.

findings.title: Denial-cache test does not prove the cache short-circuits
findings.body:
The test claims to "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but it seeds `permCache` with `{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`. A false value is not a grant in `checkPermission`.

The default fake store also returns no permissions. So the request would be denied even if the denial cache were ignored, and the test passes regardless of whether `permDenialCache` works.

The cached value should be `true`, and ideally the test should assert the store was not called.
